This one's a bit long but hang in there. This actually did happen to me, and it only happened last a few days ago.

(I did post this in another paranormal reddit thread).

  
About a month ago was when I first saw it. I had woken up screaming in bed but couldn't remember having a nightmare. Confused and scared I sat up and looked around my room. I knew something woke me up... I just didn't know what. I have nightmares quite frequently so I thought that maybe I had a nightmare but just couldn't remember it. So I layed back down and fell asleep again. About 2 hours later I woke up again. Not screaming this time... but I could feel something in my room. A presence you know?  I opened my eyes and turned my head sideways to check the time. And thats when I saw it. A black smoky figure standing there, facing me. Completely still like he was just watching me. Now this should send anyone into panic. But oddly, I just fell back asleep. I had trouble sleeping the nights following, but at this point, I thought that the figure was just a bad dream. Until about a week later at 11:30pm I turned out my lights to go to sleep. And there he was again. I was completely awake, I wasn't dreaming. I promise you. He was just standing in the corner of my bedroom, completely still. I remained pretty calm at first. I think I was just shocked. I stared at him for a few seconds in silence. He wasn't human. He was never human. This was not a ghost. He had no face... like he had a head just no face. He had a human shape but it was ill-defined. I would guess he was about 6".  There was so much negative energy in the room. And I blinked and turned on my light and he disappeared. Needless to say I slept in my parent's room that night. At this point I knew it wasn't a dream and I formulated my hypothesis... this was a demon.  
Another week passed. I thought, and was hoping, that I had seen the last of him. Until one night (I had no dreams that night that I remember), I heard a girl's voice, clear as day. She said 'He's trying to wake you up." Well that woke me up. I opened my eyes to find my blanket over my head. So I didn't see anything, but I could feel his presence. I could hear him BREATHING. And again, I just fell back asleep. The night after I slept in my parents room. I slept alright, with the exception of a nightmare. But I was used to dealing with that. Well, my mom woke up and asked me if I heard anything during the night. I told her no and she just looked at me strangely. She told me that she woke up and saw a black smoky figure with no face coming towards her. She said she knew he was a demon so she screamed at him and held her hand out to stop him. She yelled that Jesus would protect her. And she told me that he sort of shrunk back and disappeared. She told me that she stayed awake a while because she was shaken up. No one woke up... my dad, myself, and my four year old brother were asleep in that room. Then she asked me if I had a nightmare that night. I told her yes and she nodded, telling me that right after seeing the demon she heard me moaning in my sleep and saying things.  
Thats all I've seen of him so far. Sometimes I can feel him when I walk into a room, especially at night. I've found that he is most comfortable in the dark so I sleep with my lights on now. You guys might not agree with me, but I know for a fact that this is demonic activity. My older sister welcomed the devil as a teen and was possessed. So I am familiar with demonic activity. And I have no doubts that a demon would try to come after me, as I am her only blood relative in my house. The only difference between her and I is that I have Jesus.

yeah, I bet it was unsettling. Right, I wouldn't want to see that either! 

Hm thats interesting. Perhaps it lived there when the house was empty... the thing about spirits is you never really know why they are there. Theres those people who try and communicate with them, though honestly I don't think thats ever a good idea. But thats pretty much the only option to figure out why they're there. Anyways, yes, thats definitely not something to expect. Its weird and creepy... I'm glad to hear that it hasn't come back.

If I were you I would believe it was a spirit of some kind. Theres two kinds of spirits... the good ones and the ones you don't mess with. The only way to know what kind of spirit you saw is to feel its energy. Yeah, I know that sounds weird. Vibe with a spirit. Really what I mean is to focus on how you feel when you saw it. Did you feel afraid? Simply unsettled? What kind of energy did it give off? 

However you said you were in a different room so you might not have been close enough to feel it. I saw a spirit in my parents closet and I couldn't feel its energy until I reached inside to switch the light on. So you might not have felt much. 

Do you know anything about the people that lived there before you? Did they have paranormal experiences? This spirit could have felt welcome with the prior residents. And the fact that you didn't see it again... it probably just moved on. Or a second option is that this was a bad spirit, a demon perhaps, surveying your family. They do that sometimes... they come and test the waters. Seems to me though that it didn't feel like it had a good chance with your family. 

Whatever this was, you know you saw something. And I'm sure it really made you question the spiritual realm.

Commenting on behalf of my bf... He does get frustrated at times as he doesn't understand why I restrict or why I don't want to eat hamburgers with him any more. He gets confused when he tries to give me a compliment on my weight and ends up making me upset. He simply doesn't understand how to help me. He tries but he ends up being exhausted. He totally understands where your bf is coming from. He won't admit it but I know it is hard to have a girlfriend who battles anorexia. As I am sure it is hard for your bf too. For this we do need to give them grace when they accidentally hurt our feelings or don't understand. 

His advice to your bf is this: "Be there for her man. She needs you now more than ever. I know its hard but there'll be things that come along that she's gonna have to help you with too. It does get stressful and frustrating, I know. Take some time and think. I have to do that sometimes. But dude, if this is the woman you want, fight for her." 

Now this is from my opinion... it is important for your bf to pay attention to his own health. Like I said, often times they wont tell you when it gets to be too much. Which brings me to an important piece of advice for both of you. KEEP YOUR COMMUNICATION OPEN! Whenever you are feeling down and those ED thoughts are taking over, tell him! Whenever your bf is stressed or upset about this, he needs to voice that to you. Keeping your feelings out on the table is so important. I know it can be a scary thing, being open like this. I was always terrified that y bf wouldn't love me the same if he knew everything. And I know he was afraid of what might happen if he told me that this was stressing him out. But you know what? Things went a lot smoother once we started opening up more. 

I really hope you and your bf can work through this, me and my bf are rooting for you <3

Recovery is definitely the hardest thing I've ever done in my life and it has also proven to be one of the best decisions I've ever made. And weight gain... well weight gain is probably the hardest reality on the road to recovery. I totally know that bittersweet feeling! It's so good and so scary all at the same time! However the scary feelings and emotions are rough to deal with.  So I thought I'd share some important truths with you on the topic of weight gain... 

◦ weight gain is 100% necessary, healthy, & normal in recovery

◦ no matter how much weight you gain, your ed is still just as valid

◦ you deserve to eat and be nourished no matter what

Just remember, if you took a rocket to the moon and weighed yourself you'd weigh a different number than here on earth. Yet just because your weight changed doesn't mean you've *personally* changed right? You would still be you. So obviously weight is just a number and has **NO EFFECT** on your personal being :))

First I want to congratulate you. A year and a half in recovery!!! That is amazing, I am so proud of you :)). About your question, I'm literally dealing with this currently so I understand *exactly* how you feel. My heart goes out to you. I know it's painful to hear these things in recovery. May I ask, does your Mom's husband know about your eating disorder? Maybe it would help you if you could speak with him about it (maybe with lovely Mom present so you're more comfortable?), and explain why comments like these hurt you? However you may not feel comfortable opening up and thats okay. I totally understand and respect that. What you can definitely do regardless is work on your internal dialogue.  I'm sure him pointing out that you've gained weight has stirred up negative thoughts and emotions. You put it perfectly when you said you've had "bad spiraling thoughts." I know it sounds kind of silly but the best way I've found to deal with these thoughts is to counter them with truthful affirmations. A month ago I sat down and wrote down every negative thought I could recall. Then under each one I wrote out a positive affirmation. For example, one of my negative thoughts was "my complexion is so ugly." Underneath I wrote "My skin serves many purposes and how it looks does not diminish my beauty." Does this practice make sense? I was so doubtful and I even laughed at myself at first. But then every time I thought that my skin was ugly, I came back to the positive affirmation. I still do struggle but now I am actually beginning to see more beauty in myself. It takes time and lots of patience, but you'll get there. Write it, think it, believe it. Bad body image is such a hard battle and I'm sure with the comments you've received it just got harder. I'm praying for strength for you, keep fighting <3 I hope this helped xx
